generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the broadleaf base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the broadleaf program gave as defaults until then.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Wikipedia (read 2026-10-17): Sida typically unlobed, Abutilon mostly unlobed, Hibiscus entire or lobed, Malva palmately lobed; Malvaceae page: often palmately lobed or compound. DELTA (read 2026-10-17) covers Malvaceae in the narrow sense (Malvoideae) and calls the blade usually palmatifid; for the broad APG family (Grewioideae, Sterculioideae, Dombeyoideae, Tilia mostly unlobed) we weighted toward none.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Wikipedia Malvaceae (read 2026-10-17): margin may be entire; when toothed, a vein runs into each tooth (malvoid teeth). Wikipedia Sida: usually serrated edges; Abutilon: wavy or serrated; Tilia: toothed in all species; Hibiscus: entire or lobed. Weighted toward the toothed herbs and shrubs (Sida, Abutilon, Pavonia, Hermannia, Grewia).

traits.stamens.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 355, 359: stamens 5 to many, filaments usually joined into a tube round the ovary or in 5 to 15 bundles. Book writes ∞ (numerous); 200 is our stand-in for the upper bound and 20 for 'numerous' with no stated lower bound.

traits.carpels.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 355, 359: carpels 2 to many, rarely 1; typical 5 is from Floral Diagrams p. 220 (general formula G (2-3) 5 to many). Book writes ∞; 50 is our stand-in for the upper bound.

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 355, 505: flowers hypogynous, rarely perigynous. Simpson p. 505 defines hypogynous and epigynous as flowers without a hypanthium.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), families 117 Sterculiaceae, 119 Bombacaceae (the baobab) and 120 Malvaceae, which APG joins with the lindens as Malvaceae: leaves alternate, simple or digitate, mostly palmately veined; stipules present, often falling early; flowers regular; sepals (3-)5, joined, valvate, often with an epicalyx; petals 5; stamens many, often in a column; ovary superior; fruit a capsule, or splitting into its carpels (cocci).

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 355, 356, 357, 358, 359, family Malvaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral, usually; read as {"spiral": "usually"}.

traits.leaf_division.note: Wikipedia Malvaceae (read 2026-10-17): leaves often palmately lobed, sometimes compound. The biggest genera it names (Hibiscus 434, Pavonia 291, Sida 275, Ayenia 216, Dombeya 197) all have simple blades; palmately compound leaves are mainly in the bombacoid trees (Ceiba, Pachira, Adansonia, Bombax), a few hundred species at most out of ~4,225. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.inflorescence.note: Flora of China Malvaceae s.s. (iplant.cn PDF, read 2026-10-17): flowers mostly single in the leaf axils, less often in small cymes or clusters, at times gathered into end racemes or panicles; genus accounts read there: Abutilon (~200 spp; single, paired or small cymes), Sida (100-150; single or paired, often in racemes/panicles), Malva (~30), Alcea (~60), Lavatera (~25) all single or fascicled in the axils. Genus sizes from Wikipedia (Hibiscus ~430, Grewia 275, Dombeya ~200; their pages read 2026-10-17 do not describe flower grouping). Counted solitary: Abutilon, Sida, Malva, Alcea, Lavatera, Althaea, Malvastrum (~490) plus the earlier pass's Hibiscus and Pavonia (~720, Wikipedia Malvaceae) against cymose Grewioideae/Byttnerioideae/Dombeyoideae (Grewia, Dombeya, Ayenia, Hermannia; ~900-1,000). Margin modest, so often against sometimes. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 355, 356, 357, 358, 359, family Malvaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite (rarely monoecious or polygamous), usually; read as {"hermaphrodite": "usually"}.
